test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 08 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: As per the Economic Survey 2024–25, what corpus amount has been launched under the Self‑Reliant India (SRI) Fund for MSMEs?
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹50,000 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Self-Reliant India (SRI) Fund** was established to provide financial support to **Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)**, emphasizing their importance in the Indian economy.
 
• Under the **Economic Survey 2024–25**, the government announced a corpus of **₹50,000 crore** for the SRI Fund to boost MSMEs.
 
• The fund aims to ensure **ease of access to equity financing** for MSMEs, facilitating their expansion and innovation.
 
• This initiative aligns with the vision of **Aatma Nirbhar Bharat**, enabling MSMEs to become globally competitive and self-reliant.
 
• The SRI Fund will focus on creating opportunities for MSMEs in sectors such as **manufacturing, technology, and exports**, contributing to sustainable economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Role of MSMEs in India:**

 
 
• **Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises** are a vital segment of the Indian economy, contributing around **30% to India's GDP**.
 
• They employ approximately **11 crore people**, making them the second-largest employment generator after agriculture.
 
• MSMEs account for nearly **48% of India’s exports**, playing a crucial role in the global supply chain.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the SRI Fund:**
 
 
• The fund will provide **equity support** to MSMEs, enabling them to scale operations without the burden of debt financing.
 
• It is implemented through professional fund managers and institutions to ensure efficient allocation of resources.
 
• The SRI Fund is expected to generate **employment opportunities** and enhance technological capabilities within MSMEs.
 
 
 
• **Government's Vision for MSMEs:**
 
 
• The government aims to make MSMEs the backbone of the **Aatma Nirbhar Bharat** initiative by fostering innovation, enhancing productivity, and ensuring global competitiveness.
 
• Policy reforms such as **collateral-free loans**, production-linked incentives (PLI), and simplified compliance requirements have been introduced to support MSMEs.
 
 
 
• **Other Important Schemes for MSMEs:**
 
 
• **Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme:** Provides collateral-free credit to MSMEs to encourage entrepreneurship.
 
• **Udyam Registration:** A simplified process for MSMEs to register and avail benefits under government schemes.
 
• **Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP):** Aims to generate employment opportunities through MSME projects.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Challenges faced by MSMEs:**

 
 
• **Limited access to credit:** MSMEs often struggle to secure loans due to high collateral requirements.
 
• **Technological gaps:** Many MSMEs operate with outdated technology, affecting their competitiveness.
 
• **Regulatory compliance:** Complex regulations and high compliance costs can hinder MSME growth.
 
 
 
• **Future Outlook:**
 
 
• The SRI Fund is expected to boost MSME contributions to India’s GDP and exports, driving the nation’s economic growth.
 
• With the right support, MSMEs can become key players in sectors such as **renewable energy, e-commerce, and advanced manufacturing**.
